bibl.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: In this paper, we present a network and training strategy that relies on the strong use of data augmentation to use the available annotated samples more efficiently.

span.label: biomedical image segmentation
span.quote: However, in many visual tasks, especially in biomedical image processing, the desired output should include localization, i.e., a class label is supposed to be assigned to each pixel.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We provide the full Caffe[6]-based implementation and the trained networks4.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: overlap-tile prediction with mirrored extrapolation at the border: the missing context outside the image is manufactured by reflecting the image itself, so a tile can be segmented without the network ever seeing beyond the edge
span.quote: To predict the pixels in the border region of the image, the missing context is extrapolated by mirroring the input image. This tiling strategy is important to apply the network to large images, since otherwise the resolution would be limited by the GPU memory.

span.label: the paper's claim that this teaches invariance WITHOUT annotating the transformations is made in the introduction, not in this span; tagged separately or not at all
span.term: elastic deformation of the training images, generated from random displacement vectors on a coarse 3 by 3 grid, sampled from a Gaussian with 10 pixels standard deviation and interpolated to per-pixel displacements with bicubic interpolation
span.quote: We generate smooth deformations using random displacement vectors on a coarse 3 by 3 grid. The displacements are sampled from a Gaussian distribution with 10 pixels standard deviation. Per-pixel displacements are then computed using bicubic interpolation.

span.label: the size of that weight - w0 = 10 - is stated in a different sentence and is not claimed here
span.term: a per-pixel loss weight, pre-computed from each ground truth segmentation by morphological operations, that both compensates class frequency and forces the network to learn the small separation borders introduced between touching cells
span.quote: We pre-compute the weight map for each ground truth segmentation to compensate the different frequency of pixels from a certain class in the training data set, and to force the network to learn the small separation borders that we introduce between touching cells (See Figure 3c and d). The separation border is computed using morphological operations.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a large number of feature channels in the expansive path, which is what carries context from the contracting path up into the high-resolution layers and makes the architecture symmetric
span.quote: One important modification in our architecture is that in the upsampling part we have also a large number of feature channels, which allow the network to propagate context information to higher resolution layers. As a consequence, the expansive path is more or less symmetric to the contracting path, and yields a u-shaped architecture.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: batch size traded down to a single image so the input tile can be large, with the momentum raised to 0.99 so that the update still integrates many previously seen samples
span.quote: To minimize the overhead and make maximum use of the GPU memory, we favor large input tiles over a large batch size and hence reduce the batch to a single image. Accordingly we use a high momentum (0.99) such that a large number of the previously seen training samples determine the update in the current optimization step.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: initial weights drawn so that each feature map starts at approximately unit variance, which is what stops one path through the network from saturating while another never contributes
span.quote: In deep networks with many convolutional layers and different paths through the network, a good initialization of the weights is extremely important. Otherwise, parts of the network might give excessive activations, while other parts never contribute. Ideally the initial weights should be adapted such that each feature map in the network has approximately unit variance.

span.label: Because convolutions are unpadded, border pixels are lost at every layer and feature maps must be cropped before concatenation.
span.note: what this limits: every output map's extent relative to its input: THE CROPPING IS NECESSARY DUE TO THE LOSS OF BORDER PIXELS IN EVERY CONVOLUTION
span.quote: The cropping is necessary due to the loss of border pixels in every convolution.

span.label: Without the overlap-tile strategy the resolution the network can handle is bounded by GPU memory.
span.note: what this limits: application to large images: THIS TILING STRATEGY IS IMPORTANT ... SINCE OTHERWISE THE RESOLUTION WOULD BE LIMITED BY THE GPU MEMORY
span.quote: This tiling strategy is important to apply the network to large images, since otherwise the resolution would be limited by the GPU memory.

span.label: Part of what the network is trained to detect is inserted by the authors: the separation borders between touching cells are synthesised, not annotated.
span.note: what this limits: a comparison of this network's boundary accuracy against a method trained on unmodified ground truth: the separation borders between touching cells are introduced by the authors and computed with morphological operations, so the two are trained on different targets
span.quote: and to force the network to learn the small separation borders that we introduce between touching cells (See Figure 3c and d). The separation border is computed using morphological operations

span.label: How heavily those borders count is set by two chosen constants in the loss.
span.note: what this limits: the segmentation scores reported here: the pixel-wise loss weight that forces border learning is controlled by two values the authors chose, w0 = 10 and a sigma of about 5 pixels
span.quote: In our experiments we set w0 = 10 and σ ≈ 5 pixels

span.label: The invariances the network has are the ones the augmentation supplied, and the paper says the corpus never contained them.
span.note: what this limits: a claim that this network is robust to deformation: the invariance was taught by applying elastic deformations during training, and the paper states the annotated corpus did not need to contain those transformations at all
span.quote: This allows the network to learn invariance to such deformations, without the need to see these transformations in the annotated image corpus

span.label: the ground truth - PARTLY SYNTHESISED: the annotation is augmented with separation borders computed by morphological operations so that touching instances can be pulled apart, so the target is the annotation plus an artefact of the method
span.quote: We pre-compute the weight map for each ground truth segmentation to compensate the different frequency of pixels from a certain class in the training data set, and to force the network to learn the small separation borders that we introduce between touching cells (See Figure 3c and d). The separation border is computed using morphological operations

span.label: very few images - AS THIRTY, AND THEN AS PATCHES: the electron-microscopy training set is 30 images, and the paper notes that in patches the training data is much larger than the image count suggests
span.quote: The training data is a set of 30 images (512x512 pixels) from serial section transmission electron microscopy of the Drosophila first instar larva ventral nerve cord

span.label: invariance - AS A PROPERTY OF THE AUGMENTATION: what the network is invariant to is what was applied to the training images, not what was observed in the microscopy
span.quote: As for our tasks there is very little training data available, we use excessive data augmentation by applying elastic deformations to the available training images

span.quote: outperforms the prior best method (a sliding-window convolutional network)

span.quote: requires many thousand annotated training samples

span.quote: In this paper, we build upon a more elegant architecture, the so-called “fully convolutional network” [9].

span.label: extends → the fully convolutional network of Long et al. [9]
span.quote: We modify and extend this architecture such that it works with very few training images and yields more precise segmentations; see Figure 1.

span.label: contradicts → the sliding-window patch strategy of Ciresan et al. [1]
span.quote: Obviously, the strategy in Ciresan et al. [1] has two drawbacks.

span.label: 7 — test-time averaging over rotated inputs
span.quote: The u-net (averaged over 7 rotated versions of the input data)

span.label: A U-shaped fully-convolutional network — a contracting path for context plus a symmetric expanding path for precise localization — trains end-to-end from very few images using heavy data augmentation.
span.quote: The architecture consists of a contracting path to capture context and a symmetric expanding path that enables precise localization.

span.label: U-Net won the ISBI 2015 cell-tracking challenge (phase-contrast and DIC microscopy) by a large margin and beat the prior sliding-window best on ISBI neuronal-structure segmentation.
span.quote: we won the ISBI cell tracking challenge 2015 in these categories by a large margin
